z3_encoding: EnumSort NodeType {Assign,Call,Name,Constant}; const nodeType; predicate (nodeType == Assign). Over the seeded enum the equality is solver-trivial: TRUE-check=sat (nodeType=Assign), FALSE-check=sat (nodeType=Call). This proves both branches are *reachable for some enum value*, but NOT that an input controls them.

true_examples.note: ast.parse("x = 1").body[0] has type(node).__name__ == "Assign" -> elif at line 692 taken

false_examples.note: ast.parse("foo(1, 2)").body[0] has type(node).__name__ == "Expr" -> falls through to a different elif (not Assign)
a bare Name expression node; nodeType=="Name" != "Assign"

rationale: nodeType = type(node).__name__ where node is a live Python AST node from ast.parse() on a config expression string, recursively dispatched in ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate. The branch is selected by the structural type of the parsed tree node, not by any cli/yaml/int/bool scalar input the solver can range over. This is parsed-tree nodeType dispatch (step 3) => runtime-dependent / solver_status=unknown. z3 over the seeded enum confirms both outcomes are reachable but cannot prove an input forces either; witnesses are given BY VALUE via real ast.parse output. Note the real AST also produces node types outside the seeded 4-value enum (e.g. "Expr", "Module", "BinOp"), so the false side is the open complement of {"Assign"}.
